settings.headline: Does it hurt?
settings.subhead: Most aesthetic treatments cause brief, manageable discomfort rather than real pain — and it varies by treatment, area and person. Here's an honest guide, treatment by treatment.
settings.image_alt: Senseless Comfort Cream and Comfort Spray — calm preparation

settings.headline: Honest comfort, treatment by treatment
settings.body: How much a treatment hurts is personal — it varies with the treatment itself, the area being worked on, and your own sensitivity. Numbing is preparation for comfort, not part of the treatment, and most practitioners apply their own as standard, so it's always worth a quick word with yours first. Compare treatments below, then go deeper on the one you're booked in for.

settings.label: Microneedling
settings.note: A light scratching or prickling — what changes it, by depth and area.

settings.label: Laser hair removal
settings.note: A quick elastic-band snap — what changes it, by area and session.

settings.label: Lip filler
settings.note: A brief sharp scratch and some pressure — eased by the numbing most practitioners use.

settings.label: Botox
settings.note: A quick pinch or sting — many people manage without any numbing.

settings.label: Microblading
settings.note: Light scratching and some pressure — usually mild, with numbing throughout.

settings.label: Lip blush
settings.note: Uncomfortable rather than painful — a scratching, tickling sensation.

settings.label: Waxing
settings.note: A brief, sharp sting as the strip is removed — it fades quickly.

settings.label: Electrolysis
settings.note: A brief heat or stinging at each hair, more noticeable on sensitive areas.

settings.heading: Not sure which to choose?
settings.body: Answer three quick questions — treatment, skin and session length — and we'll point you to the format and strength we'd reach for.

settings.label: What numbing does
settings.value: Topical numbing reduces discomfort during a treatment; it doesn't remove all sensation.

settings.label: What comfort depends on
settings.value: The treatment, the area, your skin, and how the product is applied.

settings.label: Formats
settings.value: Cream, gel and spray — matched to the area and appointment.

settings.label: Before you use it
settings.value: Patch test about 24 hours before first use and follow your practitioner's guidance.

settings.question: Does numbing cream stop all pain?
settings.answer: No — numbing cream reduces discomfort rather than removing all sensation. It makes many aesthetic treatments more comfortable, but you may still feel pressure or movement.

settings.question: Which treatments does numbing help with?
settings.answer: It's used before procedures such as microneedling, laser and semi-permanent makeup. Match the format and strength to the area and appointment — the Senseless Selector helps you choose.

settings.question: Will I feel anything during my treatment?
settings.answer: Usually some sensation remains — numbing reduces discomfort, it doesn't remove it entirely. Your practitioner can advise what to expect for your specific treatment.

settings.question: How can I make a treatment more comfortable?
settings.answer: Apply to clean skin, patch test about 24 hours beforehand, and follow the product instructions and your practitioner's advice. Choosing the right strength for the appointment helps too.
